A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PhyGDPO study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, references, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, generated-video comparisons, and a 104-participant user study in Section 3.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds cross-evaluator, cross-backbone, and hyperparameter experiments in Section 3.2.

M1.justification: The specified PGR mapping for alpha_j changes from tanh in v2 Eq. (10) to sigmoid in v3 Eq. (9), and the displayed sampled training loss gains a factor m. These are local objective revisions; the data pipeline, real-video winners, groupwise framework, and LoRA-SR mechanism remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use PhyVidGen-135K, describe selecting 17K training pairs, and evaluate VideoPhy2, PhyGenBench, and the same qualitative action scenarios. The additional evaluator, backbone, and hyperparameter configurations do not introduce new datasets or task coverage.

E2.justification: V3 Figure 8 adds untuned Wan2.1-1.3B to the weightlifting comparison that contained VideoDPO, Flow-DPO, and PhyGDPO in v2 Figure 7(b). Existing quantitative comparator sets are retained; the new cross-evaluations reuse previously compared methods.

E3.justification: V3 substantially extends evaluation configurations with Gemini-2.5-pro scoring, preference optimization on Vcrafter2, and controlled one-parameter-at-a-time sweeps. It also revises the stated sampling budget N from 100 to 20,000. Both versions still report 17K selected pairs, so this revision does not establish that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Tables 2(e–f) test dependence on the VLM evaluator and generalization to another video backbone. New Table 3 tests sensitivity to six reward hyperparameters. These substantially broaden robustness analysis beyond the retained component ablations; splitting the existing visual cases into separate figures is principally presentation.

E5.justification: V3 first states that all Table 1(c) preference estimates have 95% confidence intervals no wider than ±2.4 percentage points. V2 reports percentages without uncertainty. The interval calculation is unspecified, and neither version establishes additional repeated training runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 2(a–d) retain their numerical results, but substantial new results appear in Tables 2(e–f) and 3. Gemini scoring gives PhyGDPO 0.5525 versus Sora2's 0.5373; Vcrafter2 with PhyGDPO scores 0.1426 versus 0.1373 with VideoDPO. These are additional configurations, not same-setting improvements over v2. Hyperparameter sensitivity scores and an untuned-model visual result are also added.

T1.justification: V3 corrects the intermediate log-sigmoid sign and missing group-size factor in v2 Eq. (9), and changes the Gaussian log-ratio coefficient from h/(2 epsilon) to h²/(2 epsilon). These repair mathematical consistency within the retained derivation. The appendix's inequality statement and proof are substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction newly claim that real-video winners guarantee correct physics learning. V2 already used real videos as winners, but did not make this explicit learning guarantee in its main contribution framing. The central dataset, preference-optimization, efficiency, and benchmark-superiority contributions remain.

C2.justification: V3 newly argues that VLM errors affect sample richness or importance rather than supervision correctness, and explains using original prompts to avoid VLM bias. It interprets human and Gemini evaluations as evidence of genuine physics beyond evaluator agreement, and the Vcrafter2 experiment as evidence of generalization.

D1.justification: V3 specifies LoRA attachment to query, key, value, and output projections, switch implementation, and scaling factor 48. It also documents benchmark scoring components and thresholds, plus 48 user-study trials per participant, equal prompt allocation between benchmarks, and anonymous randomized presentation. These mostly disclose details absent from v2 rather than establish changed procedures.

R1.justification: V3 adds references for GPT-4, Gemini 2.5, CLIP, InternVideo2, and Video-LLaVA, while removing the GRPO/DeepSeekMath citation and associated speed-and-stability comparison. Its contrast with prior DPO shifts toward unreliable generated winners, while the broader research positioning remains.

P1.justification: V3 rewrites portions of the abstract, introduction, and method motivation, expands the LoRA explanation, and adds evaluation-metric and analysis paragraphs. The overall section order and most existing experimental discussion remain, making this localized revision rather than wholesale restructuring.

P2.justification: V3 redraws Figure 3, expands Table 2 with two panels, and adds the six-panel Table 3. V2's compact Figure 7 becomes three larger Figures 7–9 with expanded frame sequences and an additional baseline panel. This substantially reorganizes the experimental displays, although most illustrated cases are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 improves mathematical consistency and strengthens validation through independent-evaluator, cross-backbone, and sensitivity checks. Added implementation and study details also improve assessability. These gains are moderated by stronger physics-learning guarantees that the evidence does not establish, unspecified confidence-interval calculations, and a new description of eight user-study baselines although Table 1(c) lists seven competitors.
